newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ARA bunkers steady and trading healthy, Med firms.
newsitem.headline: ARA bunkers steady and trading healthy, Med firms.

text.p: ARA bunkers were steady on Wednesday, spurring reasonable trading volumes, while Mediterranean prices gained, quashing business, dealers said.

Rotterdam 380 CST fuel oil traded in the range $125-$126 fob, after an initial $1 a tonne advance of barges, induced by overnight crude gains. Prices were about $4-$5 higher than in Singapore, but the risk of gains encouraged buyers to part with their cash.
"A number of people offered their stored material a bit cheaper and we saw a second day of healthy demand," one dealer said.
Hamburg prices were also little changed. Bunker demand remained dormant.
Prices in Mediterranean ports were all up, southern France and Spain by $2 a tonne and Italy by about $3. Business was barely more than a trickle in most areas.

Fujairah bunkers were steady at $116/$118 fob. Traders said they expected the market to remain close to five year highs, albeit highs that were around the cheapest prices in the world. Demand was also fair, with about three or four large ships seeking fuel.
